Sapchopper (I41)

Region (English scoring-table region): Escann.

In a sentence: Turn orcish stragglers trapped in the Deepwoods into a fearsome clan, keep them loyal with plunder, and then venture into the most dangerous secrets of the Fey.

Narrative: High | Mission-tree length: Medium-long (22 dedicated missions, plus shared orc missions) | Mission-tree update: Base game v1.37.5.0; an older official dev diary records the design direction | Uniqueness: High | Campaign difficulty: Medium-high | Early pressure: High | Expansion capacity: High.

A band of orcs with no way out

In 1444, Sapchopper is a Green Orc clan in the Deepwoods. It follows Great Dookan and uses the Deepwoods Horde reform. Its starting ruler, Khagor, took power in 1442; the history script gives him the Bold Fighter, Conqueror, and Cruel personalities. His authority rests on war and spoils, not an established bureaucracy. A chieftain’s military strength can gather the clan, but it cannot by itself solve the problem of escaping the Deepwoods or maintaining loyalty within the clan. [Local history script]

The offline English wiki traces the clan’s beginnings to 1428: young orcs of Clan Bloody Tusk joined Greentide stragglers who had fled into the Deepwoods. A victory against the Wood Elves—and the killing of their leader—gave rise to the “Sapchopper” name and identity. The clan is both part of the Greentide’s legacy and a band of people trapped by pursuit, mist, and forest warfare. To outsiders they are invaders; to themselves they are looking for somewhere they can survive and prove their strength. [Wiki]

Fey magic makes their predicament stranger still. The wiki says the orcs were drawn into the Feyrealm, where time passed on a different scale from the Material Plane, before they returned to the Deepwoods and continued trying to break out. Its accounts differ on the year of their return. What the local 1444 start confirms is that the country still exists. The wiki’s account of the chieftain’s death and the clan’s dissolution in 1450 is later setting history, not an ending imposed on the player by the game. [Wiki] [Local history script]

Sustaining a new clan through plunder

The current file defines 22 Sapchopper-specific missions and connects them to 32 shared orc missions; the queried total of 56 also includes 2 generic missions. This campaign therefore layers a dedicated story over the broader development of the orcish people; the number 56 alone does not mean that every mission is exclusive to Sapchopper. [Local mission scripts]

The first political problem is loyalty. The missions ask the player to balance tribal autonomy against military privilege, while “Loyalty in Loot” makes occupying a rival’s capital, looting it, and laying waste to it concrete objectives. The chieftain does not unite the clan through promises of peace: he must keep producing victories and distributing their proceeds. The campaign cycles among conquest, army tradition, and tribal interests; stopping the wars can mean losing the most immediate means of holding the clan together. [Local mission scripts] [Local mission text]

The route then draws Wood Elves, other orc clans, and goblin powers into the struggle to unify the Deepwoods. The conflict is more than a change in map colors: scripts turn the trade goods in some Wood Elf provinces into slaves, and the narrative explicitly imagines orcish rule with other peoples serving it. This is coercive domination and enslavement, not ordinary taxation; neither the persecution of orcs nor “that is how war works” makes it a neutral policy. [Local mission scripts] [Local mission text]

From plunder to forest magic

Sapchopper does not rely on brute force alone. After incorporating the relevant clan, the shaman route inherits Og’s knowledge and uses forest magic, Mage Towers, and long-term modifiers to strengthen the country. Magic turns an inheritance from a hostile power into the clan’s own weapon, allowing orcish expansion to reach deeper into the structure of the forest. [Local mission scripts] [Local mission text]

Dark whispers, children’s rhymes about the “Prince,” the Hunter’s Grove, and hidden paths draw the campaign toward the Feyrealm. The final sack and rebuilding of Elynáile give this exploration a conqueror’s ending: discovery is not an attempt to leave the place unchanged, but a chance to remake an ancient site as a new center for the clan. The supernatural power and promises in the text carry risks; the strange storyline should not be presented as a cost-free, permanent increase in strength. [Local mission scripts] [Local mission text]

In practical terms, use military strength first to stabilize the clans and maintain a supply of spoils; then defeat Deepwoods rivals, absorb the shamans’ legacy, and advance between Fey influence and territorial consolidation. There is also a major turn: Sapchopper is excluded from the ordinary Deepwoods Orc formation-choice decision, but a dedicated event can change it into Tugund-Darakh (I46), adopt the Emerald Horde reform, and switch to a non-generic mission tree. This is a specific event route, not an ordinary nation-forming button that can be used at will; nor should the original 22 dedicated missions be described as permanently retained. The player must keep tribal interests, the army, and key preparations in view. This summarizes script direction, not a hands-on-tested optimal opening. [Local mission scripts] [Local event script]

Personality and recommendations

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansionism 92/100 | Authoritarianism 85/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 88/100 (100 = Magic, 0 = Artifice; theme intensity 78/100) | Pluralism 12/100.

The v2.1 values assessment is Evil (19/100), with a worsening trajectory. The provisional personality scores are Expansionism 92, Authoritarianism 85, Magic–Artifice direction 88 (intensity 78), and Pluralism 12. The values score is Evil 19 and gradually worsening. Dignity 18 / Public Benefit 38 / Recognition of Personhood 8 / Restraint 8: there are some local benefits from building up the clan, but they do not offset slave industries, the legal subordination of other peoples, and deliberate plunder. The low score is based on concrete institutions and harms, not on orc identity, conquest, or tribal government.

An official Cannor development diary once listed Sapchopper as a mission tree in development and emphasized war against elves and goblins and dangerous promises. It establishes the origin of the theme, not that every previewed detail was implemented at the time. Two sufficiently direct player accounts have not been obtained, so this entry makes no claim that “the community agrees it is easy/fun” and invents no campaign experience. [Official Cannor dev diary]

This country suits players who enjoy orcish warfare, shamans, and a dark story involving the Fey, and who are willing to accept an explicit enslavement route. Players seeking an egalitarian Deepwoods alliance or peaceful economic development should choose another country. See the evidence page for the shared-mission and formation boundary.

National ideas (reference appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and scripted effects. Traditions apply when the idea set is adopted; its seven ideas unlock in sequence as idea slots are filled; the ambition applies once all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government, and mission rewards are not folded into the values. Ideas acquired after formation do not automatically stack with the old set. Idea descriptions may recall the past or describe an intended future; they do not automatically mean that the events have already happened by 1444.

Sapchopper (I41) — Sapchopper Ideas

Traditions: Sapchopper Traditions

Effects: Leader Cost: -15%; Infantry Cost: -10%.

Idea 1: Sapchoppers

With a single swing of his greataxe, our first chieftain and once clanless orc, Kragur decapitated Ceann Celadil Drennen, shattered the Drennen elf army, and secured the name "Sapchopper".

Today, youngbloods eager to prove their worth follow our founder’s example. At the start of each battle, these brash warriors scour the battlefield searching for the enemy generals and captains. Upon sighting one, they charge forward attempting to strike them down and take their head, as Kragur once did. Success means earning a place in the clan as a true "Sapchopper" and the glory of watching the enemy flee in terror.

Effect: Morale Damage: +10%.

Idea 2: Worthy Foes Every Direction

In the time we’ve been in the Deepwoods, we’ve slaughtered the elves of Drennen, broken the advance of the Brambleskinner goblin, and routed the Cenág elves. And yet, Salla Drennen fights once more. The goblins press against us again. And Salla Cenág’s raids grow ever bolder. Clearly, we’ve not broken our foes yet.

Good. We need the challenge. Let them come and again taste Sapchopper steel. And should a warrior fall, then a youth shall take their weapon, eager to prove their skill.

Effects: Land Attrition: -10%; Reinforce Speed: +7.5%.

Idea 3: Everything Not Nailed Down

When we arrived in Escann from the depths of the Serpentspine, we were amazed by all the riches that could be plundered from even the smallest towns and villages. No longer did we have to live on scraps, as any orc under Dookanson could provide for themselves if they could swing an axe. In the Deepwoods, however, we have had to make do with less once again. There isn’t all that much to go around, so you’d better make sure you take all you can get.

Effect: Available Loot: +0.15.

Idea 4: Unending Warfare

Since the moment we entered the Deepwoods, we have not had a moment of rest. Unlike the Escanni, every single denizen of the woods knows how to wield a blade, and they have all been raised against us. All the better. We shall keep fighting, and we shall become more tenacious with each battle, more vigilant with each ambush, more brutal with each raid.

Effect: Army Tradition: +0.5.

Idea 5: Towns of Stone and Wood

As the invasion has dragged on, the orcish forces have slowly dragged to a halt. The tide of invasion has turned into raids and counter raids, and mobile war encampments have turned into palisaded settlements. Unwelcome as we may be, we live here now, and we had better act like it. There is rock and wood aplenty, and we will build our new home with them. We are here to stay.

Effect: Build Cost: -10%.

Idea 6: Legacy of the Great Invasion

The great orcish invasion was the largest army the Deepwoods had ever seen. An amalgamation of many clans, the invasion force cut through the forest and obliterated all opposition. So successful were the early advances of the warbands that latecomers to a battle had barely any work to do in picking off the stragglers. This bred an eagerness for glory in all the clans, who were always eager to get their part of the battle before it was over.

Effect: Reserves Organisation: +10%.

Idea 7: Strong Chieftains

The Greentide in Escann was shattered abruptly when Korgus was slain, the now-leaderless clans frenziedly gathering what power they could for themselves in the aftermath. This did not occur in the Deepwoods, where Korgus was always a distant figure and the clans functioned with great autonomy. By the time that news of Korgus’ death reached the forest, the unity of the clans had long since disintegrated and the chieftains warred against each other from their own autonomous domains. Though these internecine battles sapped their strength, their lack of reliance on central authority left the Deepwoods orc chiefdoms far stronger than their Escanni counterparts in the long run.

Effect: Global Autonomy: -0.05%.

Ambition: Sapchopper Ambition

Effect: Goods Produced Modifier: +10%.

Tugund-Darakh (I46) — Tugund-Darakhan Ideas

Traditions: Tugund-Darakhan Traditions

Effects: Hostile Attrition: +100%; Infantry Cost: -20%.

Idea 1: Shared Dream

Long ago, before orcs or even elves settled in Deepwoods, these fey forests covered half of Cannor and were home to a wide variety of magical creatures, including centaurs. The ancient human king Castan II Beastbane destroyed a significant portion of the Feywoods, leaving only the Deepwoods as a small remnant of former glory. But humanity's greatest sin was burning the World Tree to ashes. The goal of the Emerald Orcs is simple - become a weapon of vengeance for fey-kind, take these lands back and clear them of human conquerors.

Effect: Idea Cost: -5%.

Idea 2: Wrath of Nature

For many centuries Fey were persecuted by humans. They lost their lands and many were killed or exiled. While most of the Fey did not care, preferring to live in a never-ending cycle of feasts and holidays, a small faction of fey still remembered how humans humiliated and insulted them.

This faction of Fey called themselves the Ashentree Pact, named after the World Ashentree. These Fey hoped that Wood Elves, who were lured into these woods around 1000 AA could be used for their goals, but the Wood Elves turned out to be resistant to their magic and weren't interested in war with humans. Disappointed, the Ashentree Pact decided to wait for another chance, finally seeing their opportunity in the orcs which recently invaded the Deepwoods. With enhancements from fey magic orcs could be unbeatable in battle.

Effect: Shock Damage: +10%.

Idea 3: Legacy of the Greentide

During the Greentide a great number of orcish clans invaded the Deepwoods. Some of them were quite well-known among orcdom and had proven their worth during the Greentide. The Cursed Howl Clan were lead by one of the most renowned orcish warlords, Gordak. His clan sacked Bladekeep and the dreadful howls they performed during the pillage had given them their name. The Blackmoon Clan on the other side was famous for their battle shamans, who unleashed their magical power on the armies of humans and dwarves. The Silentblade Clan was considered somewhat dishonorable by other orcs, but they excelled in guerrilla combat, using ambushes to defeat their foes. And all of them are now part of the Emerald Horde, which now benefits greatly from their experience.

Effect: Army Tradition: +1.

Idea 4: Loyal to our Queen

The Emerald Horde is lead by the Warchief and his Queen. The Queen is always a Fey which has agreed to enter into marriage with a mortal orc and share part of her power with him, giving him incredible magical potency. They can not do so normally, but Emerald Orcs have consumed water from the Feyrealm and are attuned to fey magic and influence.

Effect: Morale of Armies: +10%.

Idea 5: Fey Courtiers

Fey may be not be useful when it comes to the clash of armies, but they can give us a good hand in administrating land conquered by the Emerald Horde. While they might be chaotic and absent-minded, their abilities as advisors are impressive.

Effect: Advisor Cost: -10%.

Idea 6: Warlock Kings

Emerald Orcs exchanged their free will for fey power, granting us a bevy of benefits. Aside from skin changes, we've become attuned to nature and many of us are capable of becoming powerful druids and rangers. But warlocks of powerful fey are the true elite of Emerald Horde society. They are the only ones who can become the leaders and rulers of the Horde, making them the first Witch-Kings in the modern era.

Effect: Prestige: +1.

Idea 7: Defenders of Tugund-Darakh

For many years, the High Warlocks of Tugund-Darakh, the land of a Thousand Trees, have enhanced their people with magic and artifacts from the Feyrealm. Their skin is now as hard as bark and provides great defence from regular weapons and firearms, while the inherent orcish strength was pushed even further, making them as strong as ogres. All these gifts were given to help orcs crush the human and orc realms in Cannor and plant a new Deepwoods in their place. It is our desire that the World Tree may be revived and, hopefully, emerald orcs will be accepted as full-fledged fey and be allowed to enter the Feyrealm, the Plane of Life and Magic, where fey hold their eternal feasts.

Effect: Infantry Combat Ability: +15%.

Ambition: Tugund-Darakhan Ambition

Effect: global_manpower_modifier: +20%.
